claims.claim: EAS is a predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000021 on Base mainnet and Base Sepolia.
EAS is a predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000021 on Optimism.
claims.note: The Base address is corroborated by eas-deploy-base (same address). The OP docs page named in the section cites the predeploy but not the address; the address is pinned from the Optimism specs repo.

claims.claim: timestamp(bytes32 data) returns (uint64) and getTimestamp(bytes32 data) returns (uint64) are EAS functions.
getTimestamp returns the stored time of the earliest stamp of a hash; stamping a hash that was stamped before reverts instead of overwriting.
claims.note: Source revert is AlreadyTimestamped on timestamp(); the section's 'the call reverts' means the stamping call.

claims.claim: getTimestamp(bytes32) on the EAS address returned the expected block times for the first EAS timestamp on Base Sepolia and Base mainnet; the read and write steps were checked only against those and against third-party transactions and a simulated call; the Optimism address has not been read by Anchor Suite; Anchor Suite has not sent a transaction itself.
claims.note: Own RPC observation, evidenced by the pinned fixtures. Optimism is deliberately absent from the evidence.

claims.claim: Anchor Suite's worker holds no key and sends no chain transaction; its only chain call is a read-only Solana getTransaction at finalized to a caller-supplied RPC.
claims.note: Repo-internal status as of the cited head.

claims.claim: The EAS contract stores only a time against the hash, and a hash that already has a stored time is not overwritten.
claims.note: EAS.sol L727-735 _timestamp(): reverts AlreadyTimestamped when _timestamps[data] != 0, else stores the time once.

claims.claim: OpenChainGraph section 20.4 defines no stamping leg, no key custody and no funding for the anchoring transaction, which is signed elsewhere; Anchor Suite's worker holds no key and sends no chain transaction. The signing and paying account is therefore the user's own.
claims.note: Own spec plus own repo header at the cited head. Applies to the EAS timestamp transaction as well: Anchor Suite has no code path that sends it.

claims.claim: A solana-memo binding is a ledger-ordering anchor like an OpenTimestamps commitment, not an RFC 3161 token, with no qualified or eIDAS status; EAS records a time against a hash.
claims.note: SPEC section 20.4 trust caveat (Solana); EAS.sol _timestamp() stores a time against the hash. The phrase 'by block N' is the generic reading of that stored time or slot, not a source quotation.

claims.claim: EAS timestamp(bytes32) takes only the data argument and _timestamp() stores only the time, so any account can stamp any hash and no caller is recorded; for Solana, without a signer pin anyone can write the same memo.
claims.note: EAS.sol L334-340 and L727-735: no caller check and no msg.sender stored.

claims.claim: The Solana Memo program takes UTF-8 instruction data and verifies that accounts provided are signers; the solana-memo binding of SPEC section 20.4 records a transaction whose Memo-program instruction data equals the anchored hash, with a named signer that signed the memo instruction.

Verification needs an RPC endpoint chosen by the verifier (Solana JSON-RPC getTransaction at finalized per SPEC section 20.4; an Ethereum JSON-RPC eth_call whose input carries the hash for EAS), and the endpoint receives that request.
claims.note: That the operator can see the hash follows from the request carrying it (EAS: the encoded getTimestamp argument); for Solana the request names the transaction signature and the memo is in the response.

claims.claim: A solana-memo verifier must fetch at finalized commitment; the Base mainnet and Base Sepolia EAS reads were made at the finalized block tag.
claims.note: Registers the finalized level only. No snapshot defines what finalized means on Base or Optimism, so none is asserted; 'treat anything less as pending' is a reader caution.

claims.claim: The receipt anchor_bindings schema has a solana-memo binding type and no binding type for an EAS timestamp on Base or Optimism.
claims.note: Repo-internal status as of the cited head; the SPEC section 20.4 text is repo-internal.

claims.claim: Anchor Suite verifies the Solana memo leg; no Base (EAS) check is built.
claims.note: Repo-internal status as of the cited head: verify_anchor_binding in src/worker.mjs has a solana-memo leg and no EAS leg.

claims.claim: A Base record depends on Base's sequencer and RPC operators and is not independent of them.
claims.note: Mandated caution under rubric v3.1 (D1, mandated cautions). It states a dependence and a denial only: no capability, address, number or built status, and no primary source is asserted for how the sequencer behaves.

not_registered.claim: Read at the chain's finalized tag and treat anything less as pending; do not read an EAS timestamp as showing who recorded the hash.
not_registered.reason: Worded in the section as cautions to the reader, not as statements of fact about the chains. No snapshot was retrieved for finality semantics of the finalized tag, so none is asserted. The Base sequencer sentence is registered separately as base-sequencer-dependence, a copy-rules caution.

The section names none and no claim is added.
